document.subtitle: Academic Project Synopsis

sections.abstract: The 'Smart Health Tracker & AI Diet Assistant' project presents an engineering solution within the AIML domain. A mobile-friendly web application where users can log their daily meals and physical activity. The system uses a computer vision / machine learning model to estimate calorie counts from uploaded food photos and provides personalized dietary recommendations and weekly nutrition summaries based on health goals. Developed by a team of 3 over a 42-day timeline, the platform incorporates rigorous architectural design, modular services, and empirical testing.

document.title: Progress Report: Smart Health Tracker & AI Diet Assistant
document.executive_summary: The Smart Health Tracker & AI Diet Assistant project has achieved 35% completion based on a single recorded weekly review, indicating a moderate development velocity that requires acceleration to meet final deadlines. sections.abstract: The 'Smart Health Tracker & AI Diet Assistant' project presents an engineering solution within the AIML domain. A mobile-friendly web app where users log meals. Uses ML to estimate calories from food photos and gives personalized dietary recommendations Developed by a team of 3 over a 56-day timeline, the platform incorporates rigorous architectural design, modular services, and empirical testing.
sections.problem_statement: College students and young professionals often avoid manual calorie entry because it is time‑consuming, yet existing diet‑tracking apps do not provide an easy way to estimate calories from a quick photo of a meal and deliver immediate, personalized guidance; this project delivers a mobile‑friendly web app that lets users capture a meal photo, receives an approximate calorie count via a pre‑trained image classifier, and returns simple, rule‑based dietary recommendations.
objectives: Build a responsive web interface with user registration/login and a meal‑logging form that accepts a photo upload and optional text description.

Integrate a pre‑trained CNN (e.g., MobileNetV2 from TensorFlow Hub) to classify the uploaded image into a Food‑101 category and map that category to an average calorie value using a static lookup table.

Implement a rule‑based recommendation engine that compares the estimated calories to a user‑defined daily goal and suggests one actionable tip per meal; validate the end‑to‑end flow with at least 20 test meals.
sections.project_scope: In-scope: Development and validation of core modules (Setup repository, CI/CD, and database schema). Tech stack includes frontend, backend, database, apis. Out-of-scope: Third-party commercial billing infrastructure and distributed multi-region clustering.

document.risk_mitigation_approach: Pre‑trained model may not deliver usable calorie estimates: Spend the first week building a minimal prototype that runs the pre‑trained model on 10‑15 sample images, logs the predicted class and maps it to an average calorie value. If error >30%, fall back to a rule‑based lookup table instead of ML for the MVP.; Undefined MVP feature list leading to scope creep: Hold a 2‑hour scope‑definition workshop today, produce a signed MVP spec with 5 user stories, assign story points, and lock all out‑of‑scope items until after the demo.
